vision: The world feels like a directed micro-adventure instead of a sandbox: the player/agent can discover, attune, and complete a three-step beacon pilgrimage with clear in-world guidance, readable feedback, and a visible completion beat.
objectives: Add a 3-stage beacon pilgrimage quest where only one beacon is active at a time and progression requires physically reaching and interacting in sequence.
Expose quest state through the bridge OBS payload (objective id, phase, completion progress) and interaction events so agent behavior can track progression without dev-only god-mode assumptions.
Improve navigation/readability by adding strong visual guidance for active vs inactive beacons (beam, emissive pulse, or equivalent) and concise HUD prompts/status feedback.
Provide a dedicated playtest controller script that can complete the pilgrimage in realistic mode (no required self.pos), with robust retarget/recovery behavior and meaningful logs.
implementationHints: Keep quest orchestration in a focused state container (e.g., quest manager object/module) invoked from main update loop; avoid scattering progression booleans globally.
Use existing perceivable tagging to make beacons discoverable by the bridge and keep IDs deterministic (beacon_1..beacon_3).
Controller should prioritize active objective beacon when perceived, otherwise roam with obstacle-aware search until reacquired.
implementationDetails: World/gameplay loop: add three beacon entities placed across distinct landmarks/chunks; each beacon must support inactive, active, and completed visual states. Interaction should only advance when interacting with the current active objective; out-of-order interactions return explicit rejection feedback.

Quest state/data shape: maintain questId, phase (intro|beacon_1|beacon_2|beacon_3|completed), activeObjectiveId, completedObjectiveIds[], progress [0..1], and recent quest events. Drain events into bridge event stream similarly to existing interaction events.

Bridge/OBS contract: include objective snapshot under OBS (e.g., objective field) with stable keys, and emit event types that allow playtest scripts to confirm advancement (objective_started/objective_completed/quest_completed/rejected). Keep backward compatibility for existing consumers.

Interaction UX: update on-screen prompt text contextually (approach/attune/out-of-order), show short status toasts, and show compact objective HUD plus a temporary completion banner or world pulse when quest completes.

Agent playtest behavior: create scripts/agent-beacon-pilgrimage.mjs (or scripts/playtest-*.mjs) that reads objective + perceived data, drives toward active beacon, triggers INTERACT near target, detects stalls, recovers with roam/search, and logs mission step transitions.
Runner compatibility: ensure ./scripts/run-agent-exploration.sh can run the new controller via AGENT_SCRIPT=... and document required env vars. Do not regress default exploration script behavior.

Validation criteria before handoff: npm run build passes; at least one end-to-end run reaches quest_completed within <=180s in realistic mode; captures show multiple beacon states over time; logs contain objective progression and at least one successful interaction at each stage.

Failure handling: if objective data is temporarily missing in OBS, controller should degrade gracefully to perception-only targeting (no hard lock). If beacon not perceived for prolonged period, re-enter roam recovery and reacquire without freezing.
